# Esophageal barium swallow

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Gastroenterology > Basics of gastroenterology > Esophageal barium swallow*

[Original Article Link](/library/D501mg)

---

## Summary

Esophageal barium swallow, also known as <u>esophagogram</u>, is a contrast-enhanced <u>X-ray</u> modality for visualizing the <u>esophagus</u>. It allows for the anatomy and function of the <u>esophagus</u> to be examined and is used in the evaluation of <u>dysphagia</u>, <u>odynophagia</u>, and <u>regurgitation</u> of undigested food particles. Along with <u>esophageal manometry</u>, it is the diagnostic modality of choice for evaluation of <u>esophageal motility disorders</u>.

---

## Indications

Barium swallow is indicated in the evaluation of the following symptoms and related conditions:




* Clinical features: dysphagia (inability to swallow or difficulty <u>swallowing</u>), odynophagia (painful <u>swallowing</u>), <u>regurgitation</u> of undigested food, noncardiac retrosternal <u>chest pain</u> (see “Differential diagnoses of <u>acute chest pain</u>” in the article on <u>Boerhaave syndrome</u>)

* Conditions

* <u>Esophageal motility disorders</u>

* <u>Esophageal diverticulum</u>

* <u>Tracheoesophageal fistula</u>

* Esophageal stenoses, constriction

* Esophagogastric <u>anastomosis insufficiency</u> or rupture

* <u>Esophageal cancer</u>

* <u>Hiatal hernia</u>, reflux disorders





> [!NOTE]
> Endoscopy should always be considered when evaluating symptoms involving the esophageal region (particularly to rule out <u>carcinoma</u>).
> References:[[1]](/library/3NaSaO)

---

## Contraindications

* Suspected <u>esophageal perforation</u> (see “Complications” below)

* Severe <u>dysphagia</u> (risk of <u>aspiration</u>)

* <u>Pregnancy</u>




We list the most important contraindications. The selection is not exhaustive.

---

## Technique/steps

### <u>Esophagram</u> via barium or gastrografin swallow




* Performed after an overnight fast

* Patient swallows solution containing barium sulfate;  (<u>radiopaque</u> heavy metal), followed by single static image

* Barium solution coats the inner lining of the <u>esophagus</u>, showing the size and shape of the <u>esophagus</u>, as well as contractions and <u>peristaltic</u> waves.

* Barium appears white on <u>x-ray</u>; <u>soft tissues</u> appear gray.

* If a perforation is suspected, gastrografin, a water-soluble contrast agent should be used in place of barium to avoid complications such as <u>mediastinitis</u>, <u>peritonitis</u>, or <u>pneumonia</u>





### Videofluoroscopy (<u>modified barium swallow</u>)




* Real-time contrast-enhanced imaging

* Patient swallows barium solution while a continuous <u>x-ray</u> beam is focused on the <u>esophagus</u>.

* Ideal for continuous evaluation of <u>swallowing</u> mechanism

* Test of choice for suspected <u>oropharyngeal dysphagia</u>





> [!WARNING]
> A barium-based contrast medium is contraindicated in suspected perforation, as leakage increases the risk of severe <u>mediastinitis</u>, <u>peritonitis</u>, or <u>pneumonia</u>.

## Complications

* Generally rare

* Abdominal <u>pain</u> and <u>constipation</u> most common; easily managed with <u>laxatives</u>

* <u>Allergic reactions</u> to barium

* <u>Aspiration</u> of barium can cause <u>hypersensitivity pneumonitis</u>

* <u>Esophageal perforation</u> with barium leakage → <u>mediastinitis</u>, <u>peritonitis</u>





References:[[3]](/library/2taT1m)[[4]](/library/Tta61m)




We list the most important complications. The selection is not exhaustive.
